brief.text:
The lead this morning is the tanker market, which is at extraordinary levels. The VLCC run from the Arabian Gulf to China (TD3C) is earning 1,287,851 USD/day on a TCE basis — time charter equivalent, the daily profit a shipowner nets on a voyage after voyage costs. A VLCC is the largest standard crude tanker, around two million barrels. Suezmax W.Africa–UKC is at 406,769 USD/day, Aframax North Sea–UKC at 481,500 and LR2 clean AG–Japan at 313,200. For anyone fixing crude cargoes, charterers' options are expensive and thin. Today's data offers at least one plausible backdrop: Maritime Executive reports satellite imagery confirming that a Houthi missile strike hit a critical component at the Saudi export hub of Ras Tanura, and Seatrade reports US forces reiterating Iran blockade warnings with a blacklist now covering 125 vessels. These may be factors; the data does not prove causation.

On prices, Brent crude fell 5.02 to 123.10 USD/bbl (-3.9%) and WTI fell 1.88 to 103.37 (-1.8%), leaving the Brent–WTI spread at 19.73. The data here does not show why crude fell. Henry Hub gas rose 9.5% to 2.76 USD/mmBtu, also unexplained in today's data. Bunker fuel — VLSFO, the main low-sulphur ship fuel — rose everywhere: Singapore 1,000.50 USD/t (+1.1%), Rotterdam 770.00 (+0.8%), Fujairah 989.50 (+0.3%), Houston 842.00 (+0.8%). Dry bulk was softer: the Baltic Dry Index, a composite of bulk carrier rates, slipped 25 points to 2,603 (-1.0%), with Capesize 5TC — the five-route average for the biggest bulkers, typically iron ore and coal — at 30,292 USD/day. Coal API2, gasoil, the dry and tanker ETFs and the diesel crack have no data today; the RBOB gasoline figure of 3.05 USD/gal is stale, not today's.

Running stories are all new this morning. The Ras Tanura strike damage is confirmed today. The Iran blockade and expanding vessel blacklist developed with the piracy warning in the Gulf of Aden. A third thread: Hellenic and gCaptain both report Russian diesel moving across the Atlantic under a US–Russia agreement, with a US senator demanding one tanker turn around.

Watch Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab transit counts — six VLCC transits at Hormuz on Oct 25, one VLCC at Bab al-Mandab on Oct 24 and 25 — since routing decisions feed straight into tonne-miles and rates. Watch whether the Russian diesel cargo discharges, which would shape product tanker trades.
